title: Add H200-specific tuning table for kernel launch configs (capability-gated)
author: Grace Kim
release_notes: - Runtime: add H200-specific kernel launch tuning table (auto-enabled only when H200 is detected); no behavior change on other GPUs.
description:
Motivation: As part of the FP8/INT8 benchmarking sprint, we started running the full matrix on newly provisioned H200 nodes and saw a consistent gap vs H100 for a subset of decode-heavy shapes (mostly INT8 GEMM and FP8 attention prefill at higher batch sizes). Profiling showed we were reusing the H100 launch config heuristics, which are safe but not always optimal on H200 due to slightly different sweet spots for occupancy/shared-mem tradeoffs under our scheduler’s mixed-workload traffic.

This PR adds an H200-specific tuning table for kernel launch configurations, guarded behind runtime capability detection. The intent is to (1) preserve deterministic behavior on existing GPUs and (2) allow H200 to pick a better default launch config without requiring per-model overrides.

What changed: 1) Add `H200TuningTable` with curated launch configs for: (a) quantized GEMM (INT8) buckets used in decode (common hidden sizes / head dims), and (b) FP8 attention prefill buckets for long-context prompt distributions. Each entry is keyed by a small “shape signature” (m/n/k buckets, head_dim, seq bucket, batch bucket) and returns `num_warps`, `stages`, `cta_tile`, and `smem_policy` (where supported). 2) Add capability detection `GpuCapabilities::is_h200()` and gate usage of the new table behind it. Detection is cached at runtime init (no per-request NVML calls). 3) Add a debug log hook (behind `RUNTIME_LOG_KERNEL_TUNING=1`) that records the selected tuning entry id for attribution in perf logs. 4) Extend unit tests around capability detection parsing and tuning-table lookup behavior (including a “no match -> fallback” test).

Capability gating: We treat “H200” as a specific device-class detection (NVML device name contains "H200" OR PCI device id is in the allowlist). If detection fails for any reason (NVML unavailable, permissions), we default to existing H100/Hopper heuristics. This is intentionally conservative for Private/on-prem installs.

Performance summary (perf-lab, single node, clocks pinned; see ENG-24813 notes for full matrix): - H200 INT8 decode GEMM microbench (common decode shapes, batch 8–32): +4–9% tokens/sec (median +6%). - H200 FP8 attention prefill (seq 2k–8k, batch 1–8): +2–5% prefill latency reduction (median -3.1%). - End-to-end hosted traffic replay (mixed prompt lengths, streaming chat): p95 TPOT improved ~2–4% on H200-only canary runs; TTFT within noise (+/- 1%).

Correctness/guardrails: No numeric changes beyond what already exists for FP8/INT8; this only changes kernel launch params. Existing drift checks remain unchanged. We also confirmed that when the tuning table has no match, we use the previous path.

Risk: Low to medium. Launch config changes can affect tail behavior and occasionally surface latent race conditions in vendor kernels. This is H200-only and falls back safely. We also added a quick “disable” knob via env var `RUNTIME_DISABLE_H200_TUNING_TABLE=1` (documented in code comments and release notes).

Testing: - Unit: `//runtime/gpu:capabilities_test`, `//runtime/kernels:tuning_table_test` - Integration (CI GPU): `quant_kernels_smoke_hopper` (runs on H100 CI, validates no behavior change) - Perf-lab: microbench suite + end-to-end streaming replay on H200 (manual, results attached in ENG-24813)

Checklist: [x] Capability-gated; [x] Safe fallback; [x] Debug logging behind flag; [x] Unit coverage; [x] No changes to default behavior on non-H200.

Notes for reviewers: The table entries are intentionally small and limited to the top buckets we observed in hosted traffic. We can expand after we stabilize the new perf-canary job and start collecting more H200 telemetry.
commits: runtime/gpu: add H200 capability detection + cache at init
runtime/kernels: introduce H200 tuning table and lookup plumbing
runtime/kernels: add debug log hook for tuning entry id (flagged)
tests: add capabilities + tuning-table lookup tests
docs: add release note + env var escape hatch comment
review_conversation:
Hiro Tanaka (review): Table approach looks good. Two requests: (1) ensure we don’t call NVML in the hot path; (2) add a clear fallback metric/log so perf attribution is easy.

Grace Kim (author): Good catch. Moved NVML detection to runtime init and cache the result in `GpuCapabilities`. Added `RUNTIME_LOG_KERNEL_TUNING=1` debug log with tuning entry id and a `fallback=true` flag when no entry matches.

Noah Patel (review): Can we avoid string matching on device name? Prefer stable IDs; also please document the escape hatch.

Grace Kim (author): Added PCI device-id allowlist first, with name match only as a secondary path. Added `RUNTIME_DISABLE_H200_TUNING_TABLE=1` escape hatch and release note blurb.

Isabella Rossi (review): Tests: please include a case for “NVML unavailable” -> fallback behavior.

Grace Kim (author): Added `CapabilitiesNvmlUnavailableFallsBack` unit test.

Julian Moore (review): Scheduler instrumentation won’t see this directly; can we ensure the perf log includes the tuning entry id when enabled?

Grace Kim (author): Yes—hooked into `perf_log_events` so benchmark ingestion can capture it when debug flag is on.

Hiro Tanaka (final): Approved. Let’s keep the table small for now and expand via data from the nightly quant canary.

Merged by Grace Kim via squash on 2025-10-10.
